note: The 7 voters of the 5-language follow-up council run (wf_f85173db-8a6). criteria and model are word for word from that run; description is the v1 text the user approved on 2026-11-12.

voters.name: Everyday engineer user
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): fast start, easy install and update, clear help and errors
Accepts: a larger download
Rejects: a runtime they must manage themselves
voters.description: A backend engineer who runs the tool many times a day while building services, often from their own scripts.

voters.name: Platform team maintainer
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): speed of adding commands, debugging and test tooling, few dependencies
Accepts: some build complexity
Rejects: a codebase only 1 team member can change
voters.description: One of the 6 developers on the platform team. Adds the new commands and fixes the tool when it breaks.

voters.name: Future new hire
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): readable code, size of the hiring pool, quality of docs and examples
Accepts: a less fashionable stack
Rejects: code that needs specialist knowledge to change
voters.description: A developer who joins the platform team in 2 years and inherits this tool with no handover from its authors.

voters.name: Release engineer
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): reproducible builds for 3 OSes from one CI, code signing on macOS and Windows, small artifacts
Accepts: longer CI builds
Rejects: per-OS build machines kept by hand
voters.description: Runs the CI pipeline that builds, signs, and publishes each weekly release for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

voters.name: Security engineer
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): supply-chain risk of dependencies, memory safety, fast toolchain patches
Accepts: fewer features
Rejects: unpinned or unaudited dependency trees
voters.description: Reviews the company's internal tools and their dependencies, and answers for any compromise that comes through them.

voters.name: Developer-experience support lead
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): the same behavior on all 3 OSes, actionable error messages, easy diagnostics from users
Accepts: a slower feature pace
Rejects: OS-specific bugs that need per-machine fixes
voters.description: Handles the tickets that engineers file when the tool fails on their laptop.

voters.name: Engineering manager (5-year owner)
voters.criteria:
Cares about (in order): total cost of ownership, staffing risk under turnover, long-term toolchain support
Accepts: a higher first build cost
Rejects: a toolchain with uncertain 5-year support
voters.description: Manages the platform team, owns its budget and hiring, and will own this tool for the next 5 years.
